refused: any float or fraction/exponent number form, including 1.0 and -0.0

rows.title: P-L0: bound-bytes predicate over one historical Preprod transaction body
rows.property: Bound-bytes predicate P-L0. There exist 582 bytes B such that BLAKE2b-256(B) = tx_id, B matches the template whose BLAKE2b-256 is template_digest (41 fixed header bytes; every container header and tag fixed), and output output_index (fixed to 1) of B pays at least threshold_lovelace lovelace to the payment key hash payment_key_hash.
rows.temporalScope: Bytes of one historical Preprod transaction
rows.publicInputs: Typed statementSchema: domain tag, predicate_digest, template_digest (fixed by value), asserted network label, historical tx_id, output_index (fixed to 1), payment key hash, threshold.
rows.anchorAndAssumptions: BLAKE2b-256 collision resistance; the template fixes the decoding path to output 1; Groth16 knowledge soundness as MCP-EXE-01. Inclusion of B in any chain is not part of this relation.
rows.freshnessValidity: Bytes are immutable; no inclusion, unspentness or finality.
rows.strategy: Direct Groth16 over BLS12-381 with a hand-written Blake2b gadget (as reported).
rows.implementationEvidence: Independent G16 audit (A-G16, sha256 62fbdee0...b238) agrees with the X1-X3/X5 relation observations as E1/E2 for this one template shape and dissents on the X6 binding design (F1 script binding keyed on entryName; F2 the circuit's predicate constant does not identify the relation, the X3 control VK carries the P-L0 constants). The G16 circuit's 166-byte statement layout is not this typed statementSchema; correspondence is not established. Evidence attaches to admission records (audit_refs chosen by each consumer), never to this row.
rows.firstBlocker: A statement encoding frozen by a non-author and an AdmissionRecord whose circuit_constants and audit_refs cover a key for this exact relation; X6-class binding redesign (G16 audit s11 items 1-3).
rows.moriartyRelation: Feeds P-M0 (MCP-PLN-02@2).
rows.experiment: Remove-the-binding control per binding constraint (MCP-REF-10); isolating derived-mutation vectors (G16 audit F5); control circuits only under key_role negative-control (MCP-REF-11).
rows.notEstablished: Inclusion on any chain; Preprod membership (network label asserted, body key 15 absent); phase-2 validity (is_valid and witnesses outside the txid); signer; output existence or unspentness; finality; any other template shape; that a circuit enforces each binding constraint of this statement schema.

A3: output_index fixed to 1 and template_digest fixed by value inside the SemanticEntry
A11: G16 audit 62fbdee0 recorded; experiment-disputed (qualified: typed statement and bundle carriage are X6-class and not approved); author vote 1, see NOTES

rows.title: One-ticket-per-credential nullifier burn
rows.property: Conditional on ticket issuance being unique per credential C: a claim must spend a custody UTxO and a ticket UTxO, i.e. a script-address UTxO with datum Ticket n where n = Blake2b(domainSep || scriptHash || C), consumed without a successor ticket output [P-SP2REC lines 16-23]; under that condition a second claim for C finds no ticket. Ticket creation is unconstrained in the captured validator source, so without that condition the property does not hold.
rows.anchorAndAssumptions: Ticket issuance uniqueness; LIN-01.
rows.strategy: Ledger-native replay record.
rows.implementationEvidence: External Preview record only (MCP-REC-01@1), author-reported.
rows.firstBlocker: A ticket-issuance minting policy that makes ticket creation unique per C; Moriarty has no credential/claim construct.
rows.moriartyRelation: Pattern for consumed-message records in bridge claims [B-REQ item 3].
rows.experiment: Two claims for the same C in one tx and across txs; both second attempts must fail.
rows.notEstablished: Uniqueness if ticket issuance itself can be duplicated. Ticket creation is not constrained by any minting policy in the captured validator source [P-REDVAL]; because n is computable from public data, a second Ticket n UTxO could be locked by anyone [INF; Recovery.Logic ticketBurnedFor not captured, GAP]. The record shows a ticket-datum UTxO created by an ordinary lock transaction (2969eb5f..., tx 2 in P-SP2REC) and an author-reported mis-encoded one (e73dfb35...#2) that the author states is undecodable: evidence of unconstrained creation, not of two valid tickets for one n.
changeReason: A12: property made conditional on unique ticket issuance; status conditional-construction (audit recommendation plus author agreement); F10 wording correction accepted as unverified by the audit
